sections.title: Murals: Biography of the City (PD)
sections.description: Philadelphia is the mural capital of the world, home to more than 4,000 community-created murals. Through conversations with muralists and community members, field visits to mural sites, and mapping neighborhood assets and histories to understand a mural's place within the neighborhood’s ecosystem, students learn how public art emerges through collaboration and shared authorship. We will create the framework for community engagement utilizing methods such as interviews and listening sessions, while learning how inclusive dialogue shapes the mural-making process. At the heart of building a mural is a process that requires inquiry, observation, and thinking together across culture and geography. The course culminates in the creation and painting of a small mural, giving students firsthand experience with dialogue-driven artmaking and a deeper understanding of how communities create shared meaning through public art. This is an SNF Paideia-designated course and is open to all Penn students, not only Paideia fellows.
